title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
summary: Replaces dense BF16 KV-cache storage and full-sequence decode attention with NVFP4 packed cache, FP4 query-key scoring over the full history, and sparse FP16 value aggregation over selected 128-token blocks. Costs include Blackwell-generation hardware (GB300-class FP4 tensor cores), calibration of key centering and up to two BF16 pages per sequence and layer, and a fixed per-head block budget that caps attended context. Accuracy losses appear at smaller budgets (64 blocks on some models), gains are demonstrated only on Blackwell hardware unavailable to most constrained setups, and speedups may not transfer to non-Hopper/Blackwell GPUs or API-served models.
rationale: The method is training-free and effective, but it requires Blackwell FP4 tensor-core hardware and custom kernel support that a 24 GB GPU or third-party API stack cannot provide, so it should be monitored until compatible kernels or hardware become accessible.

claims.statement: Replaces dense BF16 KV-cache storage and full-sequence decode attention with NVFP4 packed cache, FP4 query-key scoring over the full history, and sparse FP16 value aggregation over selected 128-token blocks. Costs include Blackwell-generation hardware (GB300-class FP4 tensor cores), calibration of key centering and up to two BF16 pages per sequence and layer, and a fixed per-head block budget that caps attended context. Accuracy losses appear at smaller budgets (64 blocks on some models), gains are demonstrated only on Blackwell hardware unavailable to most constrained setups, and speedups may not transfer to non-Hopper/Blackwell GPUs or API-served models.
Qwen3.8-27B achieves a 1.94x end-to-end decode speedup over dense BF16 at 128K context and batch size 16 on one GB300; KV pools provide 2.58-2.76x BF16's token capacity.
